name: THS4032 / THS4031 / THS4032-EP
tagline: TI's 1.6 nV/√Hz, 100 MHz comms dual that Head-Fi rollers praise for detail and imaging, despite heat and oscillation.

lineage.note: In-house TI THS design on a 30 V dielectrically isolated complementary bipolar process (multi-GHz fT). SLOS224 since July 1999.

part_numbers.note: Industrial, DGN (8-pin MSOP PowerPAD), tape and reel. ACTIVE on TI.com.
TI part-details page exists; status unconfirmed.
SOIC-8, industrial. Code inferred from TI's suffix scheme.
Commercial SOIC-8 / MSOP PowerPAD. Unconfirmed; THS4031CD and THS4031CDGNR siblings are listed.
Enhanced product (defense/aerospace) with its own datasheet; orderable and document number unconfirmed.
Single-channel sibling on the same SLOS224 datasheet.

reputation.summary: Head-Fi has a dedicated THS4032 thread, and it recurs in 'The Opamp thread'. Posters call it 'highly recommended for audio although it was not designed with audio in mind' and 'bright, detailed, clean, well separated'; one rates its imaging next to the AD797. These are rolling impressions, not measurements.
typical_uses: Op-amp rolling in DACs and headphone amps (Beresford TC7520)
I/V and output stages in DIY audio
Designed for communications, imaging, low-noise ADC buffering
caveats: Runs hot: about 8.5 mA per channel quiescent.
Can oscillate in sockets or poor layouts; 275 MHz needs tight decoupling.
SMD only (SOIC-8 / MSOP PowerPAD); rolling needs a DIP adapter.
Headline specs changed between revisions (settling 60 → 70 ns).
One reviewer found the mids thin.

counterfeit_notes: No THS4032-specific counterfeit reports found. It is SMD-only and often sold pre-mounted on DIP adapters by marketplace sellers; buy from authorized distributors and check TI markings and date codes.

silicon_changes.identification: None known. No PCN, new-die note or marking change was found; compare the datasheet revision in use.
silicon_changes.summary: No evidence of a die change; only headline specs moved. Current documents quote 70 ns settling, −96 dBc THD at 1 MHz and 1.2 nV/√Hz; older revisions gave 60 ns (confirmed), −90 dBc and 1.6 nV/√Hz (unconfirmed). Looks like re-characterisation, not new silicon.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Likely negligible for audio. Settling in the tens of ns is far beyond audio bandwidth.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low – pinout and package unchanged; no PCN; datasheet-level differences only.
silicon_changes.verification: Current 70 ns, −96 dBc and 1.2 nV/√Hz figures and older 60 ns confirmed; no PCN or die-change evidence.

revision_history.changes: First release; known only from the 'July 1999' base date on later headers.

Header 'SLOS224I – July 1999 – Revised May 2018' (likely DigiKey copy); front page still 60 ns, 90 mA.
Header 'SLOS224J – July 1999' confirmed; Feb 2024 date reported. An E2E user found J hard to find.
Inferred from an E2E post; falls between February and July 2024.
Current symlink ('SLOS224L, revised July 2024'). Front page gives 70 ns settling; changes not shown.
